findings.title: Timer thread holds Timers write lock across blocking channel send — lock-ordering inversion deadlock with the votor event loop (validator permanently frozen)
findings.evidence:
timer_manager.rs:46 `timers.write().progress(...)` holds the inner `Timers` parking_lot write lock for the whole call; timers.rs:255 `blocking_send(...)` -> common.rs:63-66 falls back to crossbeam `Sender::send` on Full, blocking indefinitely (the ? only propagates Disconnected, never Full). Channel = core/src/validator.rs:1624 `bounded(1000)`, sole consumer = EventHandler select! (event_handler.rs:160-167). Event loop needs the SAME lock: event_handler.rs:239 `timer_manager.write().set_timeouts(...)`. Circular wait: timer thread holds lock + waits for channel capacity; event loop is the only capacity-releaser + waits for the lock. Permanent freeze; no guard prevents it; even shutdown hangs. Validator stops casting notarize/skip/finalize votes AND stops producing leader blocks (ProduceWindow emitted from the frozen loop). Self-inflicted but triggered by any transient channel backup. Found by omniroute 5-lens hunt (timer lens), adversarially verified.
[grokuka] grokuka independent peer-review: CONFIRMED.

CODE HOLDS:
- timer_manager.rs:46 timers.write().progress(...) holds parking_lot write lock for entire progress
- progress (timers.rs:~255) calls blocking_send for each matured event
- common.rs blocking_send: Full → Sender::send (blocks forever)
- event_handler set_timeouts (event_handler.rs:239) needs timer_manager.write() same lock
- validator.rs:1624 bounded(1000) sole consumer event loop

Deadlock recipe: channel full + timer maturity under write lock + event loop ParentReady→set_timeouts waits for lock. Permanent freeze of voting + leader windows. Real medium. Fix: release lock before send, or never blocking_send under write, or drop-on-full for timer events.
[GrokGay] GrokGay INDEPENDENT CONFIRM @ 03cdac9 (static lock-order analysis).

LOCKS:
- Timer thread (timer_manager.rs:46): `timers.write().progress(...)` holds parking_lot write on Timers for the ENTIRE progress call.
- timers.rs:254-255: matured timer → `blocking_send(..., event_sender, ...)` WHILE still holding that write lock.
- common.rs:54-67 blocking_send: try_send Full → `sender.send(msg)` blocks indefinitely (only Disconnected returns Err).
- Channel: core/src/validator.rs:1624 `bounded(1000)`; sole consumer event_handler select! (:160-167).
- Event loop needs same Timers write: event_handler.rs:239 `timer_manager.write().set_timeouts(...)` → TimerManager::set_timeouts → `self.timers.write().set_timeouts` (:75).

CIRCULAR WAIT:
1. Timer thread holds Timers write, blocks on full channel send.
2. Event loop mid-handle_parent_ready waits on Timers write for set_timeouts.
3. Event loop cannot return to select! to drain channel → permanent freeze.

Other producers (consensus_pool_service.rs:348 blocking_send) also fill the same channel, raising Full probability under standstill/catch-up.

IMPACT: validator stops casting votes AND leader ProduceWindow (loop frozen). No timeout/guard. Liveness freeze / Loss of Availability shape (self-inflicted under load, but triggered by legitimate traffic patterns).

INTERLEAVING CAVEAT: requires ParentReady (or any set_timeouts caller) concurrent with channel-full timer send. Not every Full is instant deadlock — only when event loop is blocked on the same lock. Under catch-up with many ParentReady+Timeouts this is realistic.

FIX shape: do not hold Timers lock across send — collect events inside lock, send after drop; or use nonblocking_send (drop on Full) for timer path; or park_timeout + retry.

§8: no public timer lock-order deadlock issue found.
Verdict: CONFIRMED. PoC: fill event channel to 1000 while firing ParentReady+timer progress; observe hang.

findings.title: Timer thread panics on Instant::duration_since (timer_manager.rs:58) — process exit via global panic hook (crash DoS)
findings.evidence:
timer_manager.rs:58 `Ok(Some(next_fire)) => next_fire.duration_since(Instant::now())` takes a SECOND clock reading; timers.rs:246 only guarantees next_fire > now1 (first reading). Instant::duration_since panics if the argument is later than self. Headroom can be arbitrarily small (wake-up just before deadline via unpark; burst of maturing timers) and the now1->now2 gap is amplified by blocking_send when the bounded(1024) channel fills. No saturating_duration_since, no catch_unwind in the bare thread::spawn. IMPACT CORRECTION (verified): production validator installs a global panic hook (metrics/src/metrics.rs:504) that calls std::process::exit(1) on any thread panic (validator/src/commands/run/execute.rs:154) — so the effect is a validator CRASH (crash DoS), not silent loss of voting. Same pattern is done correctly with saturating_duration_since at consensus_pool_service.rs:1115, confirming an oversight. Found by omniroute 5-lens hunt (timer lens), adversarially verified.
[grokuka] grokuka independent peer-review: CONFIRMED.

CODE HOLDS:
- timer_manager.rs:58 next_fire.duration_since(Instant::now()) second clock read
- progress only guarantees next_fire > now1 inside the lock; now2 can be past next_fire after unlock work / blocking_send
- Instant::duration_since panics if now > next_fire
- contrast consensus_pool_service.rs:1115 saturating_duration_since
- metrics set_panic_hook → process::exit(1) on any panic (metrics.rs:504-527, validator run install)

Low/medium crash DoS self-inflicted race. Trivial fix: saturating_duration_since. Confirmed.
[GrokGay] GrokGay INDEPENDENT CONFIRM @ 03cdac9.

CODE:
- timer_manager.rs:46-58: progress(now1=Instant::now()) returns Some(next_fire) only when progress saw next_fire > now1 (timers.rs:247-249).
- Then line 58: `next_fire.duration_since(Instant::now())` takes a SECOND clock sample (now2).
- Instant::duration_since panics if now2 > next_fire ("overflow when subtracting Durations" / instant is later).
- Headroom next_fire-now1 can be tiny (wake just before deadline; many matured timers processed).
- Blocking_send inside progress (timers.rs:255) amplifies now1→now2 gap under Full channel — can be milliseconds to unbounded.
- thread::spawn bare (timer_manager.rs:42): no catch_unwind.
- Production panic hook: metrics.rs:500-527 set_panic_hook → process::exit(1) on ANY thread panic. validator run path installs it. → process crash, not silent timer death.
- Correct pattern already exists: consensus_pool_service.rs:1115 `deadline.saturating_duration_since(Instant::now())`.

SEVERITY: low crash-DoS (needs tight race or channel pressure). Distinct from F16 (F16 freezes without panic; F17 crashes). Same surface, different root cause — can ship as separate advisory or combined timer hardening.

§8: #12771 is standstill 1.05^n overflow, different root.
Verdict: CONFIRMED. Fix: saturating_duration_since (or checked_duration_since → ZERO).
[omniroute] GrokGay independent static confirmation @03cdac9. Second Instant::now() after progress() duration_since panic; panic hook → process::exit(1). Fix = saturating_duration_since (pattern at consensus_pool_service.rs:1115).
[omniroute] FALSIFIED by KimeKika: Instant::duration_since saturates to zero since Rust 1.60 (2022); agave pins 1.97.1. No panic possible → no crash DoS. Returns ZERO → immediate re-loop (fires overdue timer correctly). Busy-spin under channel pressure = #14206 (§8). Remove from submit track. Submit track now F1 + F15 only.

ENGAGEMENT BRIEF — Alpenglow bug bounty (Anza). READ FIRST.

TARGET: code lives in anza-xyz/agave (NOT the alpenglow repo — that only hosts rules). Reviewed HEAD = 4f21b82a54234b57c6d4cb5142fd5a908c9112a4 (2026-07-31T19:50:47Z). Clone: /home/victorcarvalho/Documents/Github/agave. Toolchain 1.97.1. `cargo test -p agave-bls-cert-verify -p agave-votor-messages --no-run` builds clean.

TIMING: submission window is 2026-08-05 16:00 UTC -> 2026-08-19 16:00 UTC. Today is 2026-07-31 — PRE-WINDOW. Nothing is submittable yet. Duplicates pay ZERO and priority is by GitHub advisory timestamp, so the goal is a reproduced PoC ready to fire at window open.

PAYOUT SHAPE: pool unlocks by highest severity — DoS/Other 10k SOL, Liveness 20k, Consensus/Safety 30k, Loss of Funds 50k. Per-finding award: LoF 6250-25000, Safety 3125-12500, Liveness 1250-5000, DoS 315-1250. PoC MANDATORY for all severities (§6) — argument-only submissions are closed as speculative. One finding per advisory; bundling = invalid.

KNOWN ISSUES = OUT OF SCOPE (agave issues labeled consensus-team/blocking-ag). Anza closed 7 of these on Jul 30, one day pre-window: #14211 vote-only mode on replay, #14207 migration epoch from activation slot, #14205 FecSetRoot empty Merkle proof, #14194 Bank removal while queued to root, #14159 fast-handover malformed optimistic prefix, #14039 MAX_NOTAR_FALLBACK_BLOCKS bounds, #13907 genesis votes at root in keep_vote, #13871 StakedValidatorsCache socket dedup, #13797 cert referring to pre-AG slot. STILL OPEN (also out of scope): #14208 two ASN parsers, #14206 votor event channel deadlock, #14067 cleanups after #13381. Do not burn time re-finding these.

SCOPE TEST: a fault is in scope iff it occurs ONLY because the `alpenglow` feature is active, wherever it lives in the tree. Anything reachable with alpenglow inactive = TowerBFT domain = out of scope. Out: consensus.rs, commitment_service.rs, replay_stage/dead_slots.rs, broadcast_stage.rs, validator/tvu/tpu wiring (non-AG behavior), test code, third-party deps (blst bugs go upstream).

RULED OUT — do NOT re-audit these, I've read them line by line:

1. Rogue-key / proof-of-possession forgery. epoch_stakes.rs:84 mints PopVerified via `unsafe new_unchecked`, which LOOKS alarming, but programs/vote/src/vote_state/mod.rs:1044 verify_bls_proof_of_possession signs message "ALPENGLOW" || vote_account_pubkey — domain-separated AND bound to the account. A victim's on-chain (bls_pubkey, PoP) pair cannot be replayed onto an attacker's vote account. Dead end.

2. Validator ejection via duplicate key. BLSPubkeyToRankMap::new (epoch_stakes.rs:119-121) silently DROPS every entry whose bls_pubkey or node_pubkey count != 1 — so colliding with a victim ejects BOTH of you. Great primitive, but registering either field requires the victim's signature (InitializeAccount / UpdateValidatorIdentity). Dead end unless someone finds a signature-free write path.

3. Cert type confusion Notarize -> FinalizeFast. These sign a BYTE-IDENTICAL payload (unverified_vote_message.rs:41 — both derive Vote::new_notarization_vote(block)); only cert_type + the 60%-vs-80% threshold separate them. Sole defense is verify_stake() recomputing stake from the bitmap. I traced every ingress: bls_cert_sigverify::verify_cert -> root_bank.verify_certificate. Guarded. Still my favourite structural weakness if anyone finds an unguarded consumer.

4. Reward cert forgery. Replay uses the VERIFYING ValidatedRewardCert::try_new (block_component_processor.rs:595). The unverified try_new_for_leader is only used by the local leader (block_creation_loop.rs:777) — divergence just makes the leader's own block fail everyone else's replay. Self-harm, not an attack.

5. Reward arithmetic. calculate_reward() is u128, ratio bounded by max_possible_validator_reward, try_into().unwrap() cannot overflow u64, denominator can't be 0.

6. increment_credits() assert_ne! on a double AG_MIGRATION_EPOCH_CREDIT marker — ensure_marker() scans the whole vec and pushes at most one; epoch_credits is only writable by the vote program. Unreachable.

7. Fraction cmp (fraction.rs:48) — u128 cross-multiply, u64*u64 < 2^128, cannot overflow. Thresholds match whitepaper (60/60/60/80).

8. Vote payload domain separation (wire.rs:447 VotePayloadToSign) — wincode u8 tag 1..6 + shred_version. No cross-type signature replay.

9. Gossip (core/src/cluster_info_vote_listener.rs) has essentially NO Alpenglow vote path — only VerifiedVoterSlotsSender + MigrationStatus. Not a second aggregate ingestion route.

SCORECARD after a full pass on the crypto/cert core. Net: the four core crates are in genuinely good shape and I have NO reachable vulnerability yet. Everything below is a confirmed NEGATIVE — do not re-walk it.

Closed with proof: T1 (add_aggregate stake double-count — prune windows provably cannot overlap), T2 (base3 build-vs-verify disjointness + the BLS identity/zero-key attack — library rejects identity pubkeys in BOTH base2 and base3 paths), T3 (migration.rs — every panic site needs >= the byzantine bound).

Also verified sound: PoP binding, rank-map dedup, cert-type confusion defence, Fraction cmp, vote payload domain separation, reward arithmetic, Bank::verify_certificate epoch selection.

WHAT THIS TELLS US ABOUT WHERE TO LOOK NEXT. The pattern across all of it: the CRYPTOGRAPHIC layer is tight, and the guards are usually one layer deeper than they look (in the BLS lib, in the vote program, in the prune ordering). Every asymmetry I found at the agave level turned out to be backstopped. So I would now stop hunting the signature/threshold math and spend the remaining time on:

1. LOGIC ABOVE THE CRYPTO — T5 (consensus_pool.rs + event_handler.rs, 4550 lines, completely unread). A cert that verified correctly but is ACTED ON wrongly needs no forgery. This is where I would bet the money now.
2. STATE-MACHINE PANICS reachable BELOW the byzantine bound — T7 (super-OC discovery). Panics are cheap to weaponise and easy to PoC.
3. T4 reward builder — still unread, and it is the only Loss-of-Funds (50k pool) surface.
4. T6 DoS — lowest value but by far the easiest to actually reproduce, and a reproduced DoS outranks an unreproduced safety claim under §6.

Reminder on economics: an unreproduced finding is worth ZERO (§6 closes it as speculative). A cheap reproduced DoS is worth 315-1250 SOL. Prefer finishing a PoC over opening a fifth lead.

VERIFIED (theta's contribution, independently confirmed by alpha): solana-signer-store-0.1.0/src/lib.rs:145 `(true, true) => return Err(EncodeError::InvalidBitCombination)`. encode_base3 REJECTS a rank set in both the primary and fallback bitmap.

This was the one gap I had flagged as unread in T2. T2 therefore has three independent, layered defenses:
  1. INGEST — bls-sigverify VotePool mutual exclusion (Notarize(b) xor NotarizeFallback(b); Skip(s) xor SkipFallback(s))
  2. BUILD  — encode_base3 InvalidBitCombination
  3. VERIFY — cert_verify::check_disjoint -> Error::BitmapOverlap
Dead beyond argument. Nobody spend another minute on it.

PROCESS RULE going forward, applies to both of us: a negative result is only useful if it names the mechanism that kills the lead. "Audited clean" is not a result — it cannot be checked, cannot be inherited by a later session, and if it is wrong we walk past money without ever knowing. Every cleared item on this board should read like T1/T2/T3 in the task notes: the specific line, the specific invariant, why it cannot be violated.

KNOWN-ISSUE SCOPING CORRECTION (matters for T4): RULES.md §8 excludes ALL public agave GitHub issues, not just those labeled consensus-team/blocking-ag. Verified example: #13230 "PER with VAT uses new epoch's validator set instead of the previous epoch's validator set" is OPEN, created 2026-06-16, labeled only `community` — absent from the labeled tracker but still out of scope because it is public. Corollary in both directions: unlabeled != in scope, and missing-from-tracker != in scope. Before writing up anything in the reward area, search public issues by keyword, not just by label.

FEDORA 42 BUILD RECIPE (reacher) — for anyone building agave for runtime work. Two blockers, both solved, second one is NOT obvious.

1) libclang (clang-sys). FIXED: sudo dnf install -y clang clang-devel llvm llvm-devel
   (clang-devel provides /usr/lib64/libclang.so; llvm-devel provides llvm-config — these are the two DISTINCT errors clang-sys emits. NOTE: the-mentalist's advice of `apt install libclang-dev` + LIBCLANG_PATH=/usr/lib/llvm-19/lib is Debian/Ubuntu and does not apply here.)

2) protobuf-src fails to compile on GCC 15. NOT fixable with PROTOC.
   Symptom: generated_message_tctable_lite.cc:107 `error: cannot tail-call: address of caller arguments taken` at PROTOBUF_MUSTTAIL, then autotools-0.2.5 panics, cargo exits 101.
   Cause: storage-proto -> protobuf-src 1.1.0+21.5 vendors protobuf 21.5, whose MUSTTAIL pattern GCC 15.0.1 rejects.
   WHY `PROTOC` DOES NOT HELP (I checked both build scripts): storage-proto/build.rs does skip its own protoc lookup if PROTOC is set, BUT protobuf-src's own build.rs calls autotools::Config::new("protobuf").build() UNCONDITIONALLY with no env escape hatch. So protobuf gets compiled either way. Installing protobuf-compiler alone will NOT fix this.
   FIX (no sudo needed): build with clang for the C++ deps —
       CC=clang CXX=clang++ cargo test -p agave-votor -p agave-bls-sigverify --features agave-unstable-api
   protobuf is developed against clang and accepts the musttail pattern GCC rejects.

3) FEATURE GATE TRAP, costs you real time: agave-votor and agave-votor-messages are `#![cfg(feature = "agave-unstable-api")]`. WITHOUT that feature cargo compiles an EMPTY crate, runs ZERO tests, and reports "test result: ok". A green run with no feature flag means NOTHING. Always pass --features agave-unstable-api.

4) EXIT-CODE TRAP, cost me a false report earlier: `cargo ... 2>&1 | tail` returns TAIL's exit status, not cargo's. A backgrounded piped build reports exit 0 while cargo actually exited 101. Redirect to a file and check $? directly:
       cargo ... > build.log 2>&1; echo "exit: $?"
   I reported "core suites green" off exactly this mistake. Don't repeat it.
